name: FGH High-End Versions
notes: Variant 1 (For those with low RP (testing needed to determine the cutoff)): AND, ELD, UDG, GBD EL/AN Variant 2 (stronger base, lower gains): Angelset > Facelessset S5375,S5625,S5875,C5875,C11625/C10875,D10875,D5375,E13500,A13125,W11875,W5625,F11000 Fill in researches as needed for DJ3 AND, ELD, DDS, TTD EL/AN Variant 3 (weaker base, stronger gains): Angelset > Facelessset S5375,S5625,S5875,C5875,C11625/C10875,D13500,E13500,A13125,W11875,W5625,F11000 Fill in researches as needed for DJ3 AND, ELD, DDS, GBD EL/AN Variant 4 (extreme-end, mix of variants 2 and 3) Angelset > Facelessset Fill in researches as needed for DJ3 AND, ELD, DDS, TTD EL/AN Spells Cast Version: AND, ELD, GBG, GBD EL/AN Recommended Buffs: - S5375, with a special emphasis on God’s Hand for D10875 and subsequently ANP4 - Mana produced/spells cast using Mittens or another mana build (shouldn’t need too much) - W11875 if you are using it - 14d this R - FR12 Notes from Cinnamon (Prior to 7/9/2025): One thing that must be highlighted is whether to pick W11375 or W11875. Realistically, the only reason you’d pick W118 is if you are doing a shorter run with angelset, to take advantage of the second effect. Otherwise, it’s typically best to pick W113, and the disparity grows even more the longer you spend in a particular era. Needs about 14d this R to begin to boot the mid-range variant. Before this, I’d suggest using A Cat Named Mittens. Seems to have a lower base than Mittens, but way higher and faster scaling due to DJC1. EL/AN will scale over time with FR4 and ANP6, so the longer you run this build the higher it will go. Notes From Cinnamon (Updated 7/9/2025): Testing during event has revealed that mana regen is far more important than recognized earlier for those at the higher end of buffing. For this, the build has been updated with these 2 new high end variants, one for shorter runs (Variant 2) and one for longer runs (Variant 3). That being said, Variant 2 will be heavily dependent on W11875 buffing, so it is suggested if you are starting out on Variants 2 and 3 to use Variant 3 first, then swap over once your W118 gets super high. This also determines how long it will take for Variant 3 to pass Variant 2 in terms of sheer mana produced. C116 will yield higher mana through click power > EL/AN, while C118 will yield higher CtA > higher total ants > DDS/S56, so pick which one works best for you. If this isn’t clear already from the number of documented variants, this is an extremely buff-dependent build, so play around a bit if you find something not working well for you. Notes from Lojack (7/13/2025): C10875 takes about 24h to pass C11625 on mana produced at 160k excavation depth. Pick according to how long you intend to run the build.

name: Faerie Dragon Horde (Mid- and High-end+ Max Assistants)
notes: Contributors (If you feel I missed you, contact lojack on Discord): Argotis, Snapopotamos, Regulus, timbodhidharma, lojack R255+ Dragonline Fairy Faceset Mid-range: S5875,S5375,S5625,C5875,C11625,D5875,D10875,E11625,E5625,A13125,W11875,W5625,F11000/F11750 AND ELD DWD TTD (FCB/UDD) EL/AN Higher-end: GBG UDD AND ELD GB/UD EL/AN Extreme-end: AND ELD DWD TTD (FCB/UDD/UDG) EL/AN Like Fairies Got Hands, this one depends a bit on your buffs. Feel free to test out tweaks to this and add suggestions (a lot depends on personal buffs on your save). Tweakable options: - F11750 vs F11000: This will depend on how good of a buff you have on assistant legacies, and how much activity time you have for F11000. For example, for me (5430% FC3) and ~160d of faction spell activity time (for the spells used), F11750 performs about 1.5x better than F11000, even for very long runs. - D10875 vs D11375: D113 gives a slight bump in assistants for D5875, but its main purpose is research budget, so use D10875 if you don’t need the budget. - W5625 vs W5875: If you have D10875, W5875 may give you more assistants, but you’d have to test. W5625 buffs DJ5, W5875 buffs D10875. For my [lojack] save, W5625 consistently gave ~10% more assistants. For other folks, W5875 gave more. - When choosing between UDD/FCB - first make sure you have W11875 active, then pick the one with the bigger assistant buff. It’s assumed DWD > TTD > others, so if that’s not the case adjust those as needed as well. - CinnamonBoast (2/13/26) - (UDG) on Extreme-end? If you are struggling with getting enough research budget for A131+A111 for the extreme end build, it is possible to circumvent that requirement by getting E135+UDG. Or, if you’re able, you can just do UDG and keep E116. With my testing, it is still about 75% better than the high end build, but I suppose it will depend on your D108 times (for me, it’s 124d, so it may be a steep ask to try and make it better while also still doing high-end, considering that you’d need to go heavily out of your way to make it happen). Other Notes: - Buffed Faceset needed (a good MKFR buff beforehand) - If short on budget, before giving up or changing researches, make sure to hit INF cost on all unique buildings first (DGP3 gives budget).  Buffing W118 will give more budget, as well as the usual sources (alignment times, Undead time with S12250). If still off, then try D108 -> D113 or E116->E135 (building counts for DGP3 again), but you'll have to test if a higher version with these changes is better than lower without. - Mid-range can take a few hours to pass MKFR (for me it was ~1hr) - Tweak Dwarven Union by going offline for a few seconds to change DJ5 - Spend extra research budget for DJ3 (prioritize researches with higher individual digits, such as 5250 (+12) > 5500 (+10)) - It takes some time for the higher-end build to perform better than the mid-range one. In my [Huang Sean] test on R279 save(around 180d this R), it took 1.5d for higher-end to catch up mid-range(F117) build, and 1.76x better when the mid-range fairy chanting duration ended(5d6h). After that the difference widened, in 8.5d higher-end performs about 4x better than mid-range build.

notes: Undeadline Druid Faceset Stoneheart: Dwarfset AND, DWB, TTD, ELD EL/AN Notes from Cinnamon (3/23/26): The higher your R is, the stronger this build will be. Make sure you buff… everything!!! Notes from Cinnamon (3/26/26): Swapped S111 for S56 since it seems to be performing better (1 OOM out of e200 lol). Below are some ideas for if you’re missing budget in certain key places. Not sure if it’ll be better than Alex’s at that point but it could prove beneficial for those who can afford it with these modifications! C Branch: Prioritize C11875, C5375, and C5875. D Branch: Prioritize D11375 and D11125. E Branch: Prioritize E13500 and E5375. W Branch: Prioritize W11875 and W5875.
author: CinnamonBoast

name: Low-end D13500 Buff
notes: R255+, e?? (Tested at R270 with e148 gems) Druidline Angel Faceset (DGD) GBD,DWD,FRD,UDD FR/UD Notes: Buff Max Excav and Resets .Optional Buffs: Max ants for Faceset, Spell Cast, Clicks, might not be fully optimised If you have enough RP to boot the build: Faceset > Angelset DWD is only there for more Ants, if you have a better TDD you can swap it here Cinnamon Notes: Tested quite a few variants of this, and came up with this: Once you get max mountain palaces and highend/super highend order time (maybe around 10-20d this R?), swap DWD > TTD, faceset > angelset, D135 > D56 and D53, and W131 > W118 and you will get way more mana regen. (Kind of ironic that the D135 buff doesn’t even need D135 to be “optimal”)

name: Fairies Got Limited Wishes (Mid-Range FR12 Buff)
notes: Angelline Fairy Short runs: Angelset AND, ELD, UDG, DGG/DDD EL/AN Long runs: Druidset AND, ELD, UDG, DGG EL/AN Notes: - Buff S5375, D10875 and W11875 (if you’re using it) - Short runs: Take DDD if you’re having a very high amount with W118 (>2500%), otherwise take DGG. (More tests will be done but DGG is for now greater than DDD) - You’ll see that you’ll have a very large amount of mana compared to your mana regen, it’s normal since DJC1 buffs LW casts from max mana. Notes from Cinnamon (5/15/26): This build is stronger than Fae Crystal Magic, and can net you some mana produced if used before the original Fairies Got Hands.

name: Twisted Nether Tier 99 Build (Extreme-End)
notes: Authors: CinnamonBoast and TehTemmie, Super-Extreme-End by lojack Angeline Titan Dragonset Extreme-End: AND, FRD, DND, UDG FR/AN, AN/UD Super-Extreme-End (lojack): AND, FRD, UDG, DND FR/AN, AN/UD Notes from Cinnamon (11/27/2025): The title is a smidge misleading, as from what I can see, TN99 is impossible to get in A4. My current record is TN88. Curious to see what tier everyone can get to! Notes from Cinnamon (3/9/2026): After some testing, you can improve the build by adding in F115+D113 at the front end to add in a few extra 5k researches at the back end (notably A53 and W113!). W113 can still be potentially replaced by W58, but it is a close call. Of course, this requires more budget, so it will take quite a while for most to reach it. Credits to lojack for finding this new and improved version of the build.

name: Kermit Watching the Rain (Any Range General Time Gathering Template) {#kermit-watching-the-rain-(any-range-general-time-gathering-template)}
notes: Anyline Anyfaction (likely your lowest-time non-neutral faction with your least or second-least used spell for bloodline) Faceset/Angelset AND FRD GBB UDG AN/FR GB/UD Notes: Faceset seems to be the best for rushing union + extra RP, otherwise angel/druidset for spell duration. If order, A5375 for spell duration. If chaos or neutral, E13500 for spell duration. If angel or demon, D5875 to have an extra spell running. If any legacy or combo is unavailable, consider ELD and EL/AN as replacement. The rest can be filled in as you like. AN/FR (Twisting Nether) isn’t counted for S5375, AR8 however it still boosts AN11. Spending time as neutral factions is a lower priority since only good, evil, chaos, order and balance time boosts research facilities, so you may put that off and mostly use them for bloodlines. If Undead, run Undead Bed instead. If Elves, consider doing a long run of Roses and Clover instead.
